evidence: Figure 2 depicts a typical GPU architecture
Each GPC is a collection of multiple Thread Processing Clusters (TPCs)
Each TPC includes a small number of Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs)

summary: LithOS is a first-step GPU operating system that manages GPU resources at fine granularity — including a TPC-level spatial scheduler, transparent kernel atomization, hardware right-sizing, and power management — to improve isolation and utilization for ML workloads. Figure 2 is a background diagram (not LithOS-specific) that explains the hardware hierarchy LithOS operates on: HBM and an L2 cache feed a General Processing Cluster (GPC) built from a grid of Thread Processing Clusters (TPCs), each holding two Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs). A dashed connector zooms one SM into a magnified callout showing its L0 instruction cache, register file, warp scheduler, CUDA cores, tensor cores, and L1 cache/shared memory. Nested, color-coded boxes (yellow memory, blue TPCs, orange SMs, green SM internals) make the containment hierarchy explicit, giving readers the hardware vocabulary needed to follow LithOS's TPC-granular scheduling and atomization mechanisms.
